issues.legal_issue: An auction purchaser may be required to pay a previous owner's unpaid electricity dues where the sale terms disclose and allocate those dues to the purchaser and the applicable supply conditions require clearance before electricity is supplied.
material_facts: The former owner failed to pay electricity charges, and a secured creditor auctioned the unit to recover its debt.

The auction notice described the sale as being on an as-is, without-recourse basis, disclosed outstanding local-government dues including electricity bills, and stated that the purchaser would bear statutory dues and that the authorised officer would not be responsible for electricity dues.
The sale deed's indemnity covered specified losses arising from defects in title and did not extend to electricity arrears.
The auction purchaser sought a new electricity connection to operate the unit. The electricity distributor refused supply because of the former owner's unpaid electricity dues.
The applicable supply conditions allowed the distributor to refuse a new or existing connection until dues were cleared.

The lower courts had quashed the demand, relying on decisions in which the sale terms did not specifically address electricity dues or the applicable rules did not require a fresh-connection applicant to clear them.
issues.conclusion: The distributor was entitled to demand payment of the former owner's electricity arrears from the auction purchaser. The appeal was allowed and the orders quashing the demand were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Electricity dues imposed under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the terms and conditions of supply have a statutory character and are not merely contractual; Section 56 of that Act is in pari materia with Section 24 of the Electricity Act, 1910. Hyderabad Vanaspathi Ltd. v. A.P. State Electricity Board supports the statutory character of such dues. Under Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Paramount Polymers (P) Ltd. and Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited v. DVS Steels and Alloys Private Limited, a supplier may require outstanding dues to be cleared where the applicable terms so provide, and a clearance condition is not per se arbitrary or unreasonable. Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board, Haryana State Electricity Board v. Hanuman Rice Mills, Special Officer, Commerce, NESCO v. Raghunath Paper Mills, and Southern Power Distribution Company of Telangana Limited v. Gopal Agarwal involved materially different circumstances, including the absence of specific sale-term disclosure or rules requiring clearance for a fresh connection. Where the auction terms specifically disclose electricity dues and allocate statutory dues to the purchaser, and the supply conditions cover the connection sought, the purchaser may be required to clear the arrears.

rule.if: auction_purchaser_seeks_electricity_supply and prior_owner_left_electricity_arrears and sale_notice_discloses_electricity_dues and sale_terms_allocate_statutory_dues_to_purchaser and sale_is_as_is_without_recourse and supply_terms_require_clearance_for_the_connection_sought

predicates.auction_purchaser_seeks_electricity_supp: An auction purchaser sought electricity supply to use the purchased property.
predicates.prior_owner_left_electricity_arrears: The previous owner left unpaid charges for electricity supplied to the property.
predicates.sale_notice_discloses_electricity_dues: The auction notice disclosed that electricity dues were outstanding.
predicates.sale_terms_allocate_statutory_dues_to_pu: The sale terms stated that the purchaser would bear statutory dues relating to the property.
predicates.sale_is_as_is_without_recourse: The property was offered for sale on an as-is basis without recourse.
predicates.supply_terms_require_clearance_for_the_c: The applicable supply conditions required outstanding dues to be cleared before the type of connection sought could be supplied.

issues.definition: When an auction purchaser seeks electricity supply, the former owner left electricity arrears, the sale notice disclosed them, the sale terms placed statutory dues on the purchaser and were on an as-is, without-recourse basis, and the supply conditions required clearance for the connection sought, the distributor may require the purchaser to pay those arrears.
